def: The analyzer software's own computed state about a capture: indices, pairing tables, transaction groupings, queue maps, bookmarks and annotations. Interpretation, not captured traffic.
A text, CSV or XML rendering of one analyzer view, with chosen columns and range, produced by the vendor software for use in other tools. Faithful only for what it includes.
A continuous stretch of recorded traffic. Boundaries between segments (from trigger mode, buffer limits or overflow) are gaps: nothing between them was recorded.
A log of every copy, transfer, transformation and redaction of a piece of evidence, each with a cryptographic hash, so a finding can be traced to an unmodified original.

A timebase with its own offset, drift and resolution, such as the analyzer timebase, the host monotonic clock or the device's power-on time. Timestamps from different domains cannot be compared directly.
An event recorded by two evidence sources with a known identity (for example a host-logged command and its doorbell write), used to align their clocks.
Mapping one clock onto another by fitting offset and drift from anchor events; the largest residual gives the uncertainty within which cross-source order is unknown.
Events as nodes and links as edges, each edge labelled by the shared identifier (Requester ID and Tag, SQID and CID, address range, vector) and mechanism that connects them.
Comparison of a candidate run with a golden run per command-lifecycle stage (doorbell to fetch, fetch to data, CQE to MSI-X …), localizing a change to the stage and its owner.
A hash over layer-level facts of a failure (first abnormal event kind, layer, status class, absence pattern), excluding times, addresses and tags, used to group failures into triage clusters.
Everything needed to redo an analysis: input hashes, pipeline, rule and table versions, alignment parameters, configuration, outputs and their hashes.
A design in which a language model obtains facts only by calling deterministic tools (event queries, decoders, lookups) whose results carry identifiers it must cite.
The bounded amount of input a language model can attend to; a packing policy decides which events, records and passages fill it and records what was omitted.
Claims as nodes and dependencies as edges; each claim's confidence is capped by its weakest supporting claim and by rule caps such as 'no shared identifier'.
For each confidence level, the measured fraction of claims later verified true on a labelled corpus; valid only for that corpus and system version.
Text inside evidence (log strings, labels, payload decoded as text) that a language model might follow as an instruction. Countered by data/instruction separation and validator coverage rules.
A valid analysis output stating that the evidence is insufficient, with the collection that would resolve it.
Recording and fixing the model, tool and table versions used for an analysis so it can be reproduced and regressions detected.
A structured examination of a design decision: goal, invariants, options including 'do nothing', models, failure domains, observability, validation and a decision record.
A table of each option's effect on latency, throughput, CPU, memory, complexity, power and validation effort, filled with numbers or tests rather than adjectives.
A property every correct execution satisfies (for example at most one outstanding command per SQID and CID); the basis for detectors, assertions and tests.
A teaching state model of a command, transaction, error, reset or power sequence, used to reason and derive invariants; not a normative controller state machine.
The set of components or tenants affected by one fault, such as a queue pair, an interrupt vector, a function, a link or a subsystem.
Designed-in evidence — counters, logs with identifiers, tracepoints, telemetry — that makes a system's behaviour visible to forensic analysis.
A written record of a design decision: context, options considered, decision, evidence, consequences and revisit triggers.
A one-page, cited assessment of the specification changes that matter to a product, with compatibility notes and the validation work needed.
